prediction.likelyOutcome: Given conceded liability, an unrebutted (if criticized) plaintiff appraisal, and no competing government valuation, the Court of Federal Claims is likely to award the Kotis Entities substantial just compensation meaningfully below the full $44,744,774 ask but well above a nominal figure — most plausibly in the high-teens-to-thirty-million-dollar range before interest — reflecting a partial discount for credited cap-rate/comparables criticism and reduced treatment of the government's already-burdened and narrow-scope defenses as to peripheral parcels, with the anchor Core Life/Publix/Red Cinemas parcels driving most of the recovery. Interest from the October 11, 2019 taking date will add materially to whatever principal figure the court adopts.

outcome.description: After the valuation trial the Court of Federal Claims adopted Dr. Kilpatrick's before-and-after values for all thirteen parcels but struck his privacy-wall component, awarding just compensation of $42,641,740 (before values $66,179,431, after values $23,537,691) plus interest at the Moody's Aaa corporate bond rate compounded annually, against a demand of $44,744,774; it also denied the government's motion to reopen the record. No attorneys' fees were addressed in this opinion. This is the trial-level decision; no appellate ruling is reflected.
